props.gloss_en: Reuven did not sin -- whoever says he sinned is simply mistaken
as it says 'and the sons of Jacob were twelve' (Gen 35:22) -- teaching that all were equal as one
how then do I uphold 'and he lay with Bilhah his father's concubine'? it teaches that he disturbed his father's bed, and Scripture credits him as if he lay with her
is it possible that his descendants would stand on Mount Eival and say 'cursed is he who lies with his father's wife' (Deut 27:20), and this sin came to his hand?

how then do I uphold 'and he lay'? he demanded redress for his mother's humiliation: 'if my mother's sister was a rival to my mother, shall my mother's sister's maidservant be a rival to my mother?' -- he rose and disturbed her bed
Acherim: he disturbed two beds, one of the Shechina and one of his father
and that is what is written: 'then you defiled it -- he went up to my bed' (Gen 49:4): do not read yetzu'i (my bed) but yetzu'ai (my beds)
[whether Reuven sinned] is as the tannaim [dispute over 'pachaz kamayim']
R' Eliezer: [pachaz is] you were impetuous, you became liable, you acted with contempt
R' Yehoshua: you overstepped the law, you sinned, you acted promiscuously
Rabban Gamliel: you prayed, you trembled, your prayer shone forth
Rabban Gamliel: we still need the Modai['s exposition]
R' Elazar HaModai: reverse the word and expound it: you shook, you recoiled, the sin flew from you
Rava (or R' Yirmeya bar Abba): you remembered the punishment of the thing, you made yourself greatly ill, you withdrew from sinning

supports.gloss_en: שנאמר: ויהיו בני יעקב שנים עשר -- stated right after the Bilhah incident, it teaches all twelve were equal, so Reuven had not sinned
אפשר עתיד זרעו לעמוד על הר עיבל ולומר ארור שכב עם אשת אביו, ויבא חטא זה לידו? -- his descendants would not curse the very sin of their ancestor
והיינו דכתיב: אז חללת יצועי עלה -- read yetzu'ai, 'my beds', plural: two beds
